sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》（Hidden Brain）。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedanta.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆（Shankar Vedantam）。

sentences.en: In 1971, a 17-year-old girl won the Miss Black Tennessee Beauty Pageant.
sentences.zh: 1971年，一位17岁的女孩赢得了田纳西州黑人小姐选美大赛。

sentences.en: It set in motion a chain of events that would transform not just her life,
sentences.zh: 这开启了一连串的事件，不仅改变了她的人生，

sentences.en: but the lives of millions of other people.
sentences.zh: 也改变了数百万人的生活。

sentences.en: Born into poverty to a teenage mother in rural Mississippi,
sentences.zh: 奥普拉·温弗瑞（Oprah Winfrey）出生于密西西比州农村，母亲还是个十几岁的少女，她家境贫寒，

sentences.en: Oprah Winfrey had endured a difficult childhood.
sentences.zh: 度过了一个艰难的童年。

sentences.en: She bounced between relatives, experienced abuse, and left home at 13.
sentences.zh: 她在亲戚间辗转寄宿，遭受过虐待，并在13岁时离家出走。

sentences.en: The pageant became the first domino in a series of extraordinary events.
sentences.zh: 那场选美比赛成了这一系列非凡事件的第一块多米诺骨牌。

sentences.en: Her win caught the attention of WVOL, a local radio station.
sentences.zh: 她的胜出引起了当地广播电台WVOL的注意。

sentences.en: It offered her a part-time news position.
sentences.zh: 电台为她提供了一份兼职新闻工作。

sentences.en: At 19, Oprah became Nashville's first female African-American news anchor.
sentences.zh: 19岁时，奥普拉成为了纳什维尔第一位非裔美国女性新闻主播。

sentences.en: She then moved to Baltimore for television news,
sentences.zh: 随后她搬到巴尔的摩从事电视新闻工作，

sentences.en: and eventually to Chicago, where she transformed a struggling morning show into the Oprah Winfrey Show.
sentences.zh: 最终来到芝加哥，在那里她将一档收视惨淡的晨间节目改造成了《奥普拉·温弗瑞秀》。

sentences.en: I'm Oprah Winfrey, and that's what we're talking about today.
sentences.zh: 我是奥普拉·温弗瑞，这就是我们今天要讨论的话题。

sentences.en: Then came a production company, a magazine, a book club, and eventually, her own television network.
sentences.zh: 接着是制作公司、杂志、读书俱乐部，最后是她自己的电视网。

sentences.en: Oprah Winfrey became a billionaire, a household name.
sentences.zh: 奥普拉·温弗瑞成为了亿万富翁，家喻户晓。

sentences.en: For millions of people, she was the American dream made real.
sentences.zh: 对数百万人来说，她是美国梦的化身。

sentences.en: Can you see how each opportunity created momentum for the next?
sentences.zh: 你能看出每一个机会是如何为下一个机会创造动力的吗？

sentences.en: How each win opened doors that were previously closed?
sentences.zh: 每一次成功是如何打开那些曾经紧闭的大门的？

sentences.en: As the saying goes, nothing succeeds like success.
sentences.zh: 俗话说，成功带来成功。

sentences.en: But if good things can build on one another, if success can lead to more success,
sentences.zh: 但如果好事可以相互促进，如果成功可以带来更多的成功，

sentences.en: can the same thing happen the other way around?
sentences.zh: 那么反过来是否也会发生同样的事情？

sentences.en: Can setback lead to setback?
sentences.zh: 挫折是否会导致更多的挫折？

sentences.en: Failure to failure?
sentences.zh: 失败是否会导致更多的失败？

sentences.en: Can one door that is close to you turn into an endless series of obstacles?
sentences.zh: 一扇对你关闭的门，是否会演变成一连串无休止的障碍？

sentences.en: Perhaps you know people who have experienced such downward spirals.
sentences.zh: 也许你认识经历过这种恶性循环的人。

sentences.en: Perhaps you have experienced this yourself.
sentences.zh: 也许你自己也经历过。

sentences.en: The cost of downward spirals are felt most acutely by the people who experience them.
sentences.zh: 恶性循环的代价，对于身处其中的人来说感受最为深刻。

sentences.en: But all of us are made poorer by them.
sentences.zh: 但我们所有人都因此变得更加贫乏。

sentences.en: How many Oprahs do we not have today because some domino in the distant past took a spill in the wrong direction?
sentences.zh: 如果过去某个遥远的多米诺骨牌没有倒向错误的方向，今天我们会有多少个奥普拉？

sentences.en: This week on Hidden Brain and in a companion story on Hidden Brain Plus,
sentences.zh: 本周在《隐藏的大脑》节目中，以及《隐藏的大脑Plus》的配套故事里，

sentences.en: we explore the psychology of downward spirals and how our minds can set us up for failure or success.
sentences.zh: 我们将探讨恶性循环的心理学，以及我们的思想如何让我们走向失败或成功。

sentences.en: It's the kickoff to a month-long series about the mental obstacles we face
sentences.zh: 这是关于我们所面临心理障碍的系列节目的开篇，为期一个月，

sentences.en: when we try to achieve a goal or start a new chapter in our lives.
sentences.zh: 探讨当我们试图实现目标或开启人生新篇章时所遇到的阻碍。

sentences.en: Perhaps you have a New Year's resolution for yourself.
sentences.zh: 也许你为自己制定了新年计划。

sentences.en: Maybe you're struggling to keep your momentum on a work or personal project.
sentences.zh: 也许你正在努力维持工作或个人项目的进度。

sentences.en: Whatever your goal, we're going to examine why we derail our best-laid plans and how to stay on track.
sentences.zh: 无论你的目标是什么，我们都将剖析为什么我们总是破坏自己精心制定的计划，以及如何保持正轨。

sentences.en: When it rains, it pours.
sentences.zh: 祸不单行。

sentences.en: One bad thing is often followed by another.
sentences.zh: 一件坏事往往紧接着另一件坏事。

sentences.en: Your cat jumps up on the breakfast table and spills your coffee on your lap.
sentences.zh: 你的猫跳上早餐桌，把咖啡洒在了你的腿上。

sentences.en: In a bad mood, as you drive to work, you end up having a fender bender.
sentences.zh: 心情糟糕的你在开车上班途中，又发生了轻微追尾。

sentences.en: Stressed out and distracted, you now tune out during an important meeting,
sentences.zh: 压力重重且心不在焉的你，在重要会议上走了神，

sentences.en: which hurts your chances of getting that big promotion.
sentences.zh: 这损害了你获得晋升的机会。

sentences.en: The world seems to be conspiring against you.
sentences.zh: 全世界似乎都在与你作对。

sentences.en: Sometimes, these downward spirals are just a bad day.
sentences.zh: 有时，这些恶性循环只是因为倒霉的一天。

sentences.en: But other times, they can grow bigger.
sentences.zh: 但有时，它们会变得越来越严重。

sentences.en: Much bigger.
sentences.zh: 严重得多。

sentences.en: You can find yourself in a relationship that grows toxic or a job you hate.
sentences.zh: 你可能会发现自己陷入了一段有毒的关系，或者一份你讨厌的工作中。

sentences.en: Addiction, depression, and financial trouble can follow.
sentences.zh: 随之而来的可能是成瘾、抑郁和经济困难。

sentences.en: At Stanford University, Greg Walton studies the mental factors that set us up for failure
sentences.zh: 在斯坦福大学，格雷格·沃尔顿（Greg Walton）研究那些导致我们失败的心理因素，

sentences.en: and wise psychological interventions that can turn us towards success.
sentences.zh: 以及能够引导我们走向成功的明智心理干预措施。

sentences.en: Greg Walton, welcome to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 格雷格·沃尔顿，欢迎来到《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for having me.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢邀请我来。

sentences.en: Greg, I want to start by talking about self-fulfilling prophecies.
sentences.zh: 格雷格，我想先从“自证预言”谈起。

sentences.en: When you were a kid growing up in Michigan, you and your family would often go canoeing.
sentences.zh: 当你小时候在密歇根州长大时，你和家人经常去划独木舟。

sentences.en: Now, I understand that you spent quite a bit of time in boats and you were a fairly skilled paddler?
sentences.zh: 据我了解，你花了不少时间在船上，而且是一位相当熟练的划手？

sentences.en: Yes, it was like one of the big family activities we did.
sentences.zh: 是的，那是我们家的大型家庭活动之一。

sentences.en: Almost every summer, we would go on a canoe trip, often in far northern Ontario and on big rivers.
sentences.zh: 几乎每年夏天，我们都会去进行独木舟旅行，通常是在安大略省北部的大河上。

sentences.en: It was something that I love to do and I love to do as part of our family.
sentences.zh: 这是我热爱做的事情，也是我作为家庭一员热爱参与的活动。

sentences.en: I understand that you once took a canoe trip with your father on the Sturgeon River.
sentences.zh: 我听说你曾经和父亲在鲟鱼河（Sturgeon River）上进行过一次独木舟旅行。

sentences.en: I don't think I have ever visited.
sentences.zh: 我想我从来没去过那里。

sentences.en: What is this river like?
sentences.zh: 那条河是什么样的？

sentences.en: Yeah, so this is a story that he loves to tell because I am the one who am the victim of it.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是他喜欢讲的一个故事，因为我就是其中的受害者。

sentences.en: This is a small river in the northern part of the lower peninsula of Michigan.
sentences.zh: 这是密歇根州下半岛北部的一条小河。

sentences.en: It's a fast and windy river, a small, quick river.
sentences.zh: 它是一条湍急且蜿蜒的河流，一条又小又快的河。

sentences.en: And the outfitter tells you when you're renting the canoes from them
sentences.zh: 当你从租赁商那里租独木舟时，他们会告诉你，

sentences.en: that most people flip the boat on the river at one time or another.
sentences.zh: 大多数人迟早会在河里翻船。

sentences.en: And the river is quick.
sentences.zh: 而且水流很快。

sentences.en: It turns quickly.
sentences.zh: 转弯很急。

sentences.en: There's lots of overhanging branches, lots of overhanging,
sentences.zh: 有很多悬垂的树枝，有很多悬垂的……

sentences.en: lots of trees that have fallen in the river that you have to dodge.
sentences.zh: 有很多倒在河里的树，你必须躲避它们。

sentences.en: The water goes through those rushes very faSt.
sentences.zh: 水流穿过那些急流的速度非常快。

sentences.en: And if you hit them in the wrong way, the boat can turn sideways and you can fill the boat.
sentences.zh: 如果你撞击它们的方式不对，船可能会横过来，然后灌满水。

sentences.en: And there you are having an unplanned swim.
sentences.zh: 然后你就不得不进行一次计划外的游泳了。

sentences.en: So the outfitter who was walking you through this described something called sweepers.
sentences.zh: 所以，为你讲解这些的租赁商描述了一种叫做“清道夫”（sweepers）的东西。

sentences.en: I'm not much of a paddler myself.
sentences.zh: 我本人不太会划船。

sentences.en: Can you describe what a sweeper is, Greg?
sentences.zh: 格雷格，你能描述一下什么是“清道夫”吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, so if you imagine a river that's making a turn
sentences.zh: 好的，如果你想象一条正在转弯的河流，

sentences.en: and the water is rushing through the outside part of that turn
sentences.zh: 水流正急速冲过转弯的外侧，

sentences.en: and then a tree is overhanging that outside part of the turn
sentences.zh: 而一棵树正悬在转弯的外侧上方，

sentences.en: so the branches come all the way down to the water,
sentences.zh: 树枝一直垂到水面，

sentences.en: the river can sweep through very quickly, but the boat can't.
sentences.zh: 河水可以很快地流过，但船却不行。

sentences.en: The boat will get caught in the branches.
sentences.zh: 船会被树枝卡住。

sentences.en: So if you're in the main flow of the current
sentences.zh: 所以如果你处于主流中，

sentences.en: and you're in that outside flow and you hit the tree,
sentences.zh: 并且处于外侧水流中，撞上了树，

sentences.en: then you are held up, but the water keeps going.
sentences.zh: 那么你会被困住，但水流会继续前进。

sentences.en: And that's a recipe for disaster.
sentences.zh: 那简直是灾难的根源。

sentences.en: So the outfitter has basically warned you about the river.
sentences.zh: 所以租赁商基本上已经警告过你关于这条河的情况。

sentences.en: It has these sharp turns with these sweepers and your family is setting out.
sentences.zh: 它有这些带有“清道夫”的急转弯，而你们一家正准备出发。

sentences.en: I understand that you're in the boat with your dad.
sentences.zh: 我了解你当时和父亲在船上。

sentences.en: And did you exchange any notes before you set out on this journey?
sentences.zh: 在踏上这段旅程之前，你们交流过什么注意事项吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, our goal is to avoid the sweepers, right?
sentences.zh: 是的，我们的目标是避开“清道夫”，对吧？

sentences.en: So when we see the current sweeping around to the left side
sentences.zh: 所以当我们看到水流向左侧转弯，

sentences.en: and these branches hanging down, we're going to stay to the inside of those curves
sentences.zh: 并且有这些树枝垂下来时，我们会保持在弯道的内侧，

sentences.en: so that we don't get caught in the branches.
sentences.zh: 这样我们就不会被树枝卡住。

sentences.en: And as we went down the river, we saw boat after boat, you know, caught in those branches.
sentences.zh: 当我们顺流而下时，我们看到一艘又一艘船，你知道，被卡在那些树枝里。

sentences.en: And what happened?
sentences.zh: 然后发生了什么？

sentences.en: Did you get caught as well?
sentences.zh: 你们也被卡住了吗？

sentences.en: We missed every sweeper.
sentences.zh: 我们避开了所有的“清道夫”。

sentences.en: I felt very proud of myself.
sentences.zh: 我当时对自己感到非常自豪。

sentences.en: I was 10 years old and I felt like I was an accomplished canoeiSt.
sentences.zh: 我才10岁，我觉得自己像个老练的独木舟手。

sentences.en: So you're sitting at the front of the boat.
sentences.zh: 所以你坐在船头。

sentences.en: Your dad is sitting at the back.
sentences.zh: 你父亲坐在船尾。

sentences.en: You've made it through most of these sweepers.
sentences.zh: 你们已经顺利通过了大部分“清道夫”。

sentences.en: You must be feeling pretty triumphant at this point.
sentences.zh: 此时你一定感觉非常得意。

sentences.en: I'm feeling great.
sentences.zh: 我感觉棒极了。

sentences.en: And then we get to this little normal curve with no branches in sight,
sentences.zh: 然后我们到了一个普通的弯道，视野里没有树枝，

sentences.en: not even especially fast water.
sentences.zh: 水流也不是特别快。

sentences.en: And the boat is moving to the right and I feel a little jostle to the left.
sentences.zh: 船向右移动，我感觉到向左轻微的晃动。

sentences.en: And the words of the outfitter came to my mind.
sentences.zh: 租赁商的话浮现在我的脑海中。

sentences.en: 80% of people take an unplanned swim.
sentences.zh: 80%的人会进行一次计划外的游泳。

sentences.en: And so I kind of put those two parts together and I was like,
sentences.zh: 于是我把这两点联系起来，心想：

sentences.en: we're going down.
sentences.zh: 我们要翻船了。

sentences.en: I'm getting out of the way.
sentences.zh: 我得赶紧躲开。

sentences.en: So I decided to jump out of the boat to get out of the way as the boat capsized.
sentences.zh: 所以我决定跳出船，在船倾覆时避开它。

sentences.en: And of course, that's what flipped the boat.
sentences.zh: 当然，正是这个动作导致了翻船。

sentences.en: Wait, so now you're in the water.
sentences.zh: 等等，所以现在你掉进水里了。

sentences.en: Did your dad go in the water as well?
sentences.zh: 你父亲也掉进水里了吗？

sentences.en: I'm in the water.
sentences.zh: 我掉进水里了。

sentences.en: My dad's in the water.
sentences.zh: 我父亲也掉进水里了。

sentences.en: Our stuff is all floating downstream.
sentences.zh: 我们的东西都顺流漂走了。

sentences.en: My dad is sputtering at me, very upset.
sentences.zh: 我父亲对着我喷水，非常生气。

sentences.en: We end up losing like a life jacket and a spare paddle.
sentences.zh: 我们最终丢了一件救生衣和一把备用桨。

sentences.en: We spend 45 minutes retrieving our stuff and drying out.
sentences.zh: 我们花了45分钟找回东西并晾干。

sentences.en: Everybody's laughing at me.
sentences.zh: 每个人都在嘲笑我。

sentences.en: Years later, after Greg became a psychologist, it became clear to him what happened that day.
sentences.zh: 多年后，格雷格成为心理学家，那天发生的事情对他来说变得清晰起来。

sentences.en: The problem was not the river.
sentences.zh: 问题不在于河流。

sentences.en: The problem was inside his own head.
sentences.zh: 问题出在他自己的脑子里。

sentences.en: So I had the idea planted in my mind that things were going to go wrong.
sentences.zh: 我脑子里种下了一个念头，觉得事情会出错。

sentences.en: And then I was looking out for the moment when they might go wrong.
sentences.zh: 然后我一直在寻找可能出错的时刻。

sentences.en: And as soon as I saw that moment, I was like, is going wrong.
sentences.zh: 一旦我看到那个时刻，我就觉得：要出事了。

sentences.en: And I acted.
sentences.zh: 于是我采取了行动。

sentences.en: And of course, the acting is what made it go wrong.
sentences.zh: 当然，正是这个行动导致了事情真的出错。

sentences.en: So this reminds me of that classic study by the great psychologist Daniel Wegner called the White Bear Experiment.
sentences.zh: 这让我想起了伟大的心理学家丹尼尔·韦格纳（Daniel Wegner）那项经典的“白熊实验”。

sentences.en: Describe what this study was, Greg.
sentences.zh: 格雷格，描述一下这项研究吧。

sentences.en: Yeah, what Professor Wegner did was ask people not to think about a white bear and then write down their thoughts in a kind of stream of consciousness,
sentences.zh: 好的，韦格纳教授所做的是要求人们不要去想一只白熊，然后写下他们脑海中的想法，就像一种意识流，

sentences.en: like what they're thinking about for several minutes.
sentences.zh: 比如他们在几分钟内想到的事情。

sentences.en: And he finds that almost everybody references a white bear, even though that's the one thing that they're specifically not supposed to be thinking about.
sentences.zh: 他发现几乎每个人都会提到白熊，尽管那是他们明确被要求不要去想的东西。

sentences.en: That the act of suppressing it, trying to not think about it, actually calls it to mind.
sentences.zh: 压抑它的行为，即试图不去想它，实际上反而让它浮现在脑海中。

sentences.en: I mean, even as we're talking right now, I feel like I can see a ton of white bears walking across my mindscape right now.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，即使我们现在正在交谈，我也觉得我能看到无数只白熊在我的脑海中走过。

sentences.en: Exactly, right?
sentences.zh: 正是这样，对吧？

sentences.en: Don't think about it.
sentences.zh: 不要去想它。

sentences.en: And then there it is.
sentences.zh: 然后它就出现了。

sentences.en: You can't help but think about it.
sentences.zh: 你忍不住会去想它。

sentences.en: So sometimes the boat flips because the current is too strong or we're not skilled enough.
sentences.zh: 所以有时船翻是因为水流太急或者我们技术不够好。

sentences.en: But sometimes our own minds can set us up for failure.
sentences.zh: 但有时我们自己的思想也会让我们走向失败。

sentences.en: Make the connection for me between your story in the boat and the white bear study.
sentences.zh: 请为我建立一下你船上的故事与白熊研究之间的联系。

sentences.en: Yeah, so I hear the message that most people flip.
sentences.zh: 好的，我听到了大多数人会翻船的信息。

sentences.en: And I could be trying to suppress that the whole time.
sentences.zh: 而我可能一直在试图压抑这一点。

sentences.en: We're not going to flip.
sentences.zh: 我们不会翻船的。

sentences.en: We're not going to flip.
sentences.zh: 我们不会翻船的。

sentences.en: It's not going to happen to us.
sentences.zh: 这种事不会发生在我们身上。

sentences.en: We're good.
sentences.zh: 我们没问题的。

sentences.en: We're better canoeists than these other people.
sentences.zh: 我们比其他人更擅长划独木舟。

sentences.en: I know the J-stroke.
sentences.zh: 我会用J型划桨法。

sentences.en: My father knows the J-stroke.
sentences.zh: 我父亲也会用J型划桨法。

sentences.en: We're not going to flip.

sentences.zh: 于是她向妈妈哭诉：妈妈，妈妈，我有一颗牙齿松了。

sentences.en: I have a loose tooth.
sentences.zh: 我有一颗牙齿松了。

sentences.en: I'm not going to be able to go to Bucks Harbor with daddy.
sentences.zh: 我没法和爸爸去巴克斯港了。

sentences.en: And her mother then reframes it.
sentences.zh: 然后她的母亲对这件事进行了重构。

sentences.en: She says, oh, when you have a loose tooth, that's when you've become a big girl.
sentences.zh: 她说，哦，当你牙齿松动时，说明你已经长成大姑娘了。

sentences.en: And the whole first half of the book, or maybe two-thirds of the book, is about Sal kind of playing with that idea.
sentences.zh: 整本书的前半部分，或者说三分之二的内容，都是关于萨尔如何围绕这个想法展开思考的。

sentences.en: So she thinks, she asks her mother, did you have a loose tooth when you were a little girl?
sentences.zh: 她会问妈妈：你小时候牙齿松动过吗？

sentences.en: And her mother says yes.
sentences.zh: 妈妈回答说有。

sentences.en: She asks, does baby sisters, Jane's, or her tooth, will she have loose teeth too?
sentences.zh: 她问：那小妹妹简的牙齿，她也会牙齿松动吗？

sentences.en: And her mother says, not for a long time.
sentences.zh: 妈妈说，还要很久呢。

sentences.en: She's still a baby now.
sentences.zh: 她现在还是个小婴儿。

sentences.en: And then she goes to walk on the beach.
sentences.zh: 然后她去海滩上散步。

sentences.en: And she wonders whether the birds have loose teeth, whether the seal has loose teeth.
sentences.zh: 她好奇鸟儿是否有松动的牙齿，海豹是否有松动的牙齿。

sentences.en: And she gets to her father, who's digging claMs.
sentences.zh: 她走到正在挖蛤蜊的父亲身边。

sentences.en: And she proclaims, I have a loose tooth.
sentences.zh: 她宣布说：我有一颗牙齿松了。

sentences.en: I'm becoming a big girl.
sentences.zh: 我正在长成大姑娘。

sentences.en: And her father affirms that interpretation of the event.
sentences.zh: 她的父亲肯定了她对这件事的解读。

sentences.en: And then, in a sense, the denouement of the story is going to Bucks Harbor and having a great day with her father.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，故事的结局就是她去了巴克斯港，和父亲度过了美好的一天。

sentences.en: So one morning before school, your daughter Lucy sprained her ankle.
sentences.zh: 那么，在某天上学前的早晨，你的女儿露西扭伤了脚踝。

sentences.en: And she was wailing and didn't want to go to school.
sentences.zh: 她当时哭闹着不想去上学。

sentences.en: I understand that you thought of one morning in Maine as you tried to reframe the situation?
sentences.zh: 我听说你在试图重构当时的情况时，想到了《缅因州的早晨》？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, we said everybody gets a sprained ankle.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们告诉她每个人都会扭伤脚踝。

sentences.en: And it's not going to be a permanent disability.
sentences.zh: 这不会造成永久性的残疾。

sentences.en: And it's definitely not a reason not to go to school.
sentences.zh: 而且这绝对不是不去上学的理由。

sentences.en: I told her stories of my own sprained ankles.
sentences.zh: 我给她讲了我自己扭伤脚踝的故事。

sentences.en: My wife, Lisa, told stories of her sprained ankles.
sentences.zh: 我的妻子丽莎也讲了她扭伤脚踝的故事。

sentences.en: And we helped her to see that it was normal.
sentences.zh: 我们帮助她认识到这是正常的。

sentences.en: It was part of being human.
sentences.zh: 这是身为人类的一部分。

sentences.en: And it didn't have to mean anything big.
sentences.zh: 它不需要有任何重大的意义。

sentences.en: It didn't have to mean that you couldn't engage in the activities and participate in the spaces that you want to participate in.
sentences.zh: 它并不意味着你不能参与你想要参与的活动，也不能进入你想要进入的空间。

sentences.en: So in some ways, I think what this is doing is it's asking people to reconsider the possibility that the setbacks that they're experiencing are just setbacks and not catastrophes.
sentences.zh: 所以从某种程度上说，我认为这实际上是在要求人们重新审视一种可能性：他们所经历的挫折仅仅是挫折，而不是灾难。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And that fear is just as toxic as the thought, like, maybe I'm a bad kid is to a kid.
sentences.zh: 那种恐惧和“我可能是一个坏孩子”的想法对孩子来说一样具有毒性。

sentences.en: One of the other wise interventions you talk about is the power of surfacing emotions.
sentences.zh: 你提到的另一种明智干预是“显露情绪”的力量。

sentences.en: I understand that you were once visiting a museum in San Jose with your son, Oliver, when you had an opportunity to demonstrate this wise intervention.
sentences.zh: 我听说你曾经和儿子奥利弗去圣何塞的一家博物馆参观，当时你有机会展示这种明智的干预。

sentences.en: Tell me the story of what happened.
sentences.zh: 讲讲当时发生了什么事。

sentences.en: Yeah, it was the museum is tech interactive and we had gone through the whole museum.
sentences.zh: 是的，那家博物馆是“科技互动博物馆”，我们已经逛完了整个博物馆。

sentences.en: It's a great place.
sentences.zh: 那是个好地方。

sentences.en: And we had just left.
sentences.zh: 我们刚离开。

sentences.en: But Oliver was looking at an exhibit just inside the doorway.
sentences.zh: 但奥利弗还在门口内侧看一个展品。

sentences.en: So the rest of us had just walked outside of the door and he was still inside looking at this exhibit and we were waiting for him.
sentences.zh: 我们其他人刚走出门口，他还在里面看那个展品，我们在等他。

sentences.en: And then he burst out and the tears were streaming down his face and he was crying and I picked him up and I hugged him.
sentences.zh: 然后他冲了出来，泪流满面，大哭不止，我抱起他，拥抱了他。

sentences.en: And then I thought of this word surfacing.
sentences.zh: 那一刻我想到了“显露”这个词。

sentences.en: I thought to just try to say what it was that I thought he was feeling.
sentences.zh: 我想试着说出我以为他当时感受到的东西。

sentences.en: So I said, you were scared you'd be left behind, right?
sentences.zh: 所以我说：你害怕被丢下，对吗？

sentences.en: And I could feel him.
sentences.zh: 我能感觉到他。

sentences.en: He nodded and then I could just feel his body start to relax.
sentences.zh: 他点了点头，然后我能感觉到他的身体开始放松下来。

sentences.en: It was a way to kind of put the question on the table to say, I see the worry that you have.
sentences.zh: 这是一种把问题摆上台面的方式，意思是：我看到了你的担忧。

sentences.en: It's a reasonable worry.
sentences.zh: 这是一个合理的担忧。

sentences.en: And now that we both see it, we can start to let it go.
sentences.zh: 现在我们都看到了它，我们就可以开始放下它了。

sentences.en: We talked earlier about how negative spirals can become entrenched in our thinking.
sentences.zh: 我们之前谈到过负面循环是如何在我们的思维中根深蒂固的。

sentences.en: We develop fears about ourselves and then consciously or maybe unconsciously seek out evidence that confirms those fears.
sentences.zh: 我们对自己产生恐惧，然后有意识或无意识地寻找证据来证实这些恐惧。

sentences.en: These spirals then become false stories that we tell ourselves.
sentences.zh: 这些循环随后变成了我们告诉自己的虚假故事。

sentences.en: You found that having a strong personal narrative can serve as a powerful antidote to this pattern.
sentences.zh: 你发现拥有一个强大的个人叙事可以作为这种模式的有力解药。

sentences.en: You have a family story involving your grandmother that gives you a sense of identity.
sentences.zh: 你有一个关于你祖母的家庭故事，它给了你一种身份认同感。

sentences.en: What is this story, Greg?
sentences.zh: 格雷格，这个故事是什么？

sentences.en: Yeah, my grandmother is someone, this is my father's mother who I was very close with.
sentences.zh: 是的，我祖母是——这是我父亲的母亲，我和她非常亲近。

sentences.en: Her name is Vendla.
sentences.zh: 她的名字叫文德拉。

sentences.en: And in retirement in Tucson, Arizona, she wrote and self-published a couple of books, like memoirs of her life, which was quite extraordinary.
sentences.zh: 她在亚利桑那州图森市退休后，写并自费出版了几本书，比如她的人生回忆录，这非常了不起。

sentences.en: And she tells the story of how when she was 13 years old in 1922, she moved with her family from Minnesota to Arizona in a Model T Ford, how they camped along the way,
sentences.zh: 她讲述了1922年她13岁时，如何随家人开着福特T型车从明尼苏达州搬到亚利桑那州，沿途如何露营，

sentences.en: how they fixed blowouts on the tire, how they homesteaded in eastern Arizona, how they joined the ranching community there.
sentences.zh: 如何修理爆胎，如何在亚利桑那州东部开垦土地，如何加入那里的牧场社区。

sentences.en: She went to high school, how she went to high school, how she went to high school, a boarding school in Los Angeles, and then to college and became a teacher,
sentences.zh: 她如何上高中，如何去洛杉矶的一所寄宿学校上学，然后上大学并成为一名教师，

sentences.en: how she taught in one-room schoolhouses in Sedona and elsewhere in Arizona, how she met and fell in love with my grandfather,
sentences.zh: 她如何在塞多纳和亚利桑那州其他地方的单间校舍教书，如何遇见我祖父并坠入爱河，

sentences.en: how they settled in Kansas and fought through the dust storms of the Great Depression.
sentences.zh: 他们如何在堪萨斯州定居，并在大萧条的沙尘暴中奋斗。

sentences.en: It's stories of strength and agency and grit.
sentences.zh: 这些都是关于力量、能动性和坚毅的故事。

sentences.en: It's stories of goodness and community and support and neighborliness.
sentences.zh: 这些都是关于善良、社区、支持和邻里情谊的故事。

sentences.en: And there are stories that she wrote down in these memoirs.
sentences.zh: 这些故事她都写进了回忆录里。

sentences.en: And then there are also stories that she told to me personally.
sentences.zh: 还有一些是她亲自讲给我的故事。

sentences.en: And there are stories that are built into the environment.
sentences.zh: 还有一些故事是融入在环境里的。

sentences.en: So in that old homestead land in Arizona, she, as a gift, and my grandfather, received a small amount of land from the old family ranch.
sentences.zh: 在亚利桑那州那片古老的宅基地上，她和祖父作为礼物，从老家族牧场获得了一小块土地。

sentences.en: And they hand-built a cabin out of adobe.
sentences.zh: 他们亲手用土坯盖了一间小屋。

sentences.en: It's a cabin with no electricity, no running water.
sentences.zh: 那是一间没有电、没有自来水的小屋。

sentences.en: But it's become a place of family retreats and family gatherings.
sentences.zh: 但它已经成为了家庭度假和聚会的地方。

sentences.en: And to me, it represents that strength and that agency and that identity that she has.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，它代表了她所拥有的那种力量、能动性和身份认同。

sentences.en: Can you talk about how you once had a tough time in college and on Thanksgiving break, you went to visit your grandmother in Tucson?
sentences.zh: 你能谈谈你大学时曾经历过一段艰难时期，然后在感恩节假期去图森探望祖母的事吗？

sentences.en: What happened during that holiday, Greg?
sentences.zh: 那个假期发生了什么，格雷格？

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, college was, you know, discombobulating for me.
sentences.zh: 是的，大学生活对我来说，你知道，让人感到困惑。

sentences.en: It felt very far from home, very detached.
sentences.zh: 感觉离家很远，非常疏离。

sentences.en: And so there were several times I took the chance to, instead of going all the way home to Michigan, to go to Arizona and spend time with her in her retirement home.
sentences.zh: 所以有几次我抓住机会，没有回密歇根的老家，而是去了亚利桑那州，在她退休的家里陪她。

sentences.en: I would sleep on her pull-out sofa, and she would tell me stories of her experiences when she was my age, stories from when she was a boarding school student,
sentences.zh: 我会睡在她的折叠沙发上，她会给我讲她像我这么大时的经历，讲她在寄宿学校读书时的故事，

sentences.en: and stories from the cabin.
sentences.zh: 还有关于那间小屋的故事。

sentences.en: And it was a way to, you know, reconnect with those identities.
sentences.zh: 这是一种重新连接那些身份认同的方式。

sentences.en: I could see her story, and I could see her agency as she took on the challenges, as she lived through the Great Depression.
sentences.zh: 我能看到她的故事，也能看到她在应对挑战、经历大萧条时的能动性。

sentences.en: And as a young person hearing those stories, I couldn't help but hear them from the perspective of the challenges that I faced.
sentences.zh: 作为一个年轻人听到这些故事，我不禁从我所面临的挑战的角度去倾听。

sentences.en: And to think, that's how she did it.
sentences.zh: 心想，她是那样做到的。

sentences.en: How could I do it?
sentences.zh: 我该怎么做呢？

sentences.en: What's the way that I could do it?
sentences.zh: 我有什么办法能做到呢？

sentences.en: How can I be persistent?
sentences.zh: 我该如何坚持下去？

sentences.en: How can I be kind?
sentences.zh: 我该如何保持善良？

sentences.en: How can I reflect those values that are family values?
sentences.zh: 我该如何体现那些家庭价值观？

sentences.en: They're not just her values.
sentences.zh: 它们不仅仅是她的价值观。

sentences.en: They're not just my values.
sentences.zh: 它们不仅仅是我的价值观。

sentences.en: They're our values.
sentences.zh: 它们是我们共同的价值观。

sentences.en: They're who we are and who we want to be.
sentences.zh: 它们定义了我们是谁，以及我们想要成为谁。

sentences.en: Here's how she did it.
sentences.zh: 这就是她当年的做法。

sentences.en: How is it that I could do it?
sentences.zh: 我该如何做到呢？

sentences.en: Times have changed.
sentences.zh: 时代变了。

sentences.en: We're not building, you know, complicated train ticket arrangements to get from Kansas to the East Coast anymore.
sentences.zh: 我们不再需要为了从堪萨斯州去东海岸而安排复杂的火车票了。

sentences.en: We have airplanes.
sentences.zh: 我们有飞机。

sentences.en: We have different affordances.
sentences.zh: 我们有不同的条件。

sentences.en: But what are the values that are guiding us, and how can we use those to navigate our lives today?
sentences.zh: 但指导我们的价值观是什么？我们今天该如何利用这些价值观来指引我们的生活？

sentences.en: In addition to the techniques we've discussed today, there's a set of emotional tools that can make a profound difference in helping someone who's spiraling.
sentences.zh: 除了我们今天讨论的技术之外，还有一套情感工具，可以对帮助陷入困境的人产生深远的影响。

sentences.en: We talk with Greg about these tools in our companion episode, exclusively on Hidden Brain+.
sentences.zh: 我们在Hidden Brain+独家播出的配套剧集中与格雷格讨论了这些工具。

sentences.zh: 如果你是一位家长或老师，或者有朋友或伴侣陷入了负面思维循环，你一定要去看看。

sentences.zh: 如果你已经是Hidden Brain+的订阅者，该剧集现在就在这个播客订阅源中。

sentences.zh: 标题是《最好的你》。

sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅，请访问support.hiddenbrain.org。

sentences.zh: 如果你使用的是苹果设备，请访问apple.co.hiddenbrain。

sentences.zh: 再说一遍，网址是support.hiddenbrain.org或apple.co.hiddenbrain。

sentences.zh: 格雷格·沃尔顿是斯坦福大学的心理学家。

sentences.zh: 他是《平凡的魔法：我们如何通过小行动实现大改变的科学》一书的作者。

sentences.zh: 格雷格，多年来我一直想请你来节目做客。

sentences.zh: 非常感谢你今天参加Hidden Brain的节目。

sentences.en: Thank you very much, Shankar.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你，尚卡尔。

sentences.en: I really appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我真的很感激。

sentences.zh: 这是一次非常棒的谈话。

sentences.zh: 你是否有过陷入恶性循环的经历，即一件坏事接着一件坏事发生？

sentences.zh: 你是否找到过让自己摆脱负面循环的方法？

sentences.zh: 听众们分享了令人难以置信的善良故事，研究员阿比盖尔·马什（Abigail Marsh）再次做客节目，回答你们关于她极端利他主义研究的问题。

sentences.zh: 您正在收听的是“Hidden Brain”。

sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆（Shankar Vedantam）。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是“Hidden Brain”。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedanta.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: When I went to journalism school many years ago now, I noticed a certain bias in myself and many of my classmates.
sentences.zh: 多年前我上新闻学院时，注意到自己和许多同学身上存在一种偏见。

sentences.en: We wanted to do hard-hitting work, investigations.
sentences.zh: 我们想做硬核报道和调查新闻。

sentences.en: Some of us were keen to go to war zones and report from the front lines of conflict.
sentences.zh: 我们中有些人渴望去战区，从冲突前线进行报道。

sentences.en: All of us lived in dread of being relegated to so-called puff pieces.
sentences.zh: 我们所有人都害怕被分配去写所谓的“软文”。

sentences.en: A lot of stories fell into the puff piece purgatory.
sentences.zh: 很多故事都掉进了软文的炼狱。

sentences.en: Stories about cute animals.
sentences.zh: 关于可爱动物的故事。

sentences.en: Stories about insignificant local events.
sentences.zh: 关于无关紧要的本地事件的故事。

sentences.en: Stories featuring do-gooders and happy endings.
sentences.zh: 关于好心人和圆满结局的故事。

sentences.en: It's this last category that will be the focus of the rest of today's show.
sentences.zh: 正是这最后一类故事，将成为今天节目剩余部分的焦点。

sentences.en: One thing I've learned since going to journalism school is that do-gooders and happy endings actually make for great stories.
sentences.zh: 从新闻学院毕业后我学到的一件事是，好心人和圆满结局其实也能写出很棒的故事。

sentences.en: People who are extremely kind and generous can, in fact, be as fascinating as people who are extremely bad.
sentences.zh: 事实上，极其善良和慷慨的人，可以和极其邪恶的人一样引人入胜。

sentences.en: And in a time when so much of the news is disturbing, these stories remind us that kindness and decency are also to be found everywhere.
sentences.zh: 在新闻充斥着不安的时代，这些故事提醒我们，善良和体面也随处可见。

sentences.en: We talked about the heroes who walk amongst us recently with Abigail Marsh.
sentences.zh: 我们最近和阿比盖尔·马什聊到了我们身边的英雄。

sentences.en: She's a psychologist and neuroscientist at Georgetown University, and she studies extreme altruists.
sentences.zh: 她是乔治城大学的心理学家和神经科学家，专门研究极端利他主义者。

sentences.en: If you missed our first conversation with her, you can find it in this podcast feed.
sentences.zh: 如果你错过了我们与她的第一次谈话，可以在本播客订阅源中找到。

sentences.en: It's the episode titled Radical Kindness.
sentences.zh: 那期节目的标题是《激进的善良》（Radical Kindness）。

sentences.en: Abigail Marsh joins us again for our latest installment of our segment, Your Questions Answered.
sentences.zh: 阿比盖尔·马什再次加入我们，参与我们“回答你的问题”环节的最新一期节目。

sentences.en: Abigail Marsh, welcome back to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 阿比盖尔·马什，欢迎回到“Hidden Brain”。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for having me back.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢再次邀请我。

sentences.en: Abby, one of the groups of extreme altruists that you studied in your research are people who decide to donate a kidney to a stranger.
sentences.zh: 艾比，你在研究中关注的极端利他主义群体之一，是那些决定向陌生人捐赠肾脏的人。

sentences.en: And I'd like to start with a message we received after our episode aired.
sentences.zh: 我想先从我们节目播出后收到的一条留言说起。

sentences.en: It comes from listener Lucia Lloyd.
sentences.zh: 它来自听众露西亚·劳埃德（Lucia Lloyd）。

sentences.en: I really like the things that the episode was saying about how we all want to become more altruistic.
sentences.zh: 我非常喜欢这期节目中关于我们都想变得更利他的观点。

sentences.en: And I was particularly affected by the person who said that he believed that God put us on this earth to help people and wanted to do what God wanted in helping other people.
sentences.zh: 那位说他相信上帝把我们放在地球上是为了帮助他人，并想通过帮助他人来践行上帝旨意的人，让我深受触动。

sentences.en: And I thought that's what I believe too.
sentences.zh: 我想，这也是我的信仰。

sentences.en: And maybe the obvious answer to how can I be more like the people who donate their kidney to a stranger is for me to donate my kidney to a stranger.
sentences.zh: 也许对于“我该如何变得像那些向陌生人捐肾的人一样”这个问题，最直接的答案就是我也去向陌生人捐赠肾脏。

sentences.en: So I got online and started looking for how I could donate my kidney where I live.
sentences.zh: 所以我上网开始查找在我居住的地方如何捐赠肾脏。

sentences.en: And this morning made an appointment with my doctor to get the blood tests that are required to find out my blood type and have a record of that.
sentences.zh: 今天早上，我预约了医生进行必要的血液检查，以确定我的血型并留档。

sentences.en: And so I am already getting started on the process and it's too soon to know whether I will be accepted to the program, but I hope so.
sentences.zh: 我已经开始了整个流程，虽然现在说我是否会被项目录取还为时过早，但我希望如此。

sentences.en: And I wanted to let you know what a positive impact this has had on my life in motivating me,
sentences.zh: 我想让你知道，这对我的人生产生了多么积极的影响，它激励了我，

sentences.en: who had never considered donating a kidney before to go ahead and get started in the donation process and that I might very easily be ending up to save somebody's life because of your episode.
sentences.zh: 一个以前从未考虑过捐肾的人，现在开始着手捐赠流程，而且因为你们的节目，我很有可能最终挽救某人的生命。

sentences.en: So that's an incredible story, Abby.
sentences.zh: 这真是一个不可思议的故事，艾比。

sentences.en: I had tears in my eyes when I listened to Lucia's message.
sentences.zh: 听露西亚的留言时，我眼眶湿润了。

sentences.en: I hope she's able to move forward with her donation.
sentences.zh: 我希望她能顺利推进她的捐赠计划。

sentences.en: And Lucia, please keep us posted if you do.
sentences.zh: 露西亚，如果你真的去做了，请随时告诉我们进展。

sentences.en: Abby, in your work studying kidney donors, you talked with a woman who was the first known case of what is known as a non-directed donation.
sentences.zh: 艾比，在研究肾脏捐赠者的工作中，你采访过一位女性，她是已知的第一例“非定向捐赠”。

sentences.en: What is a non-directed donation and who was this woman, Abby?
sentences.zh: 什么是“非定向捐赠”？这位女性是谁，艾比？

sentences.en: First of all, I just want to take a moment to thank Lucia for calling in and telling us her story.
sentences.zh: 首先，我想花点时间感谢露西亚打来电话分享她的故事。

sentences.en: And I'm incredibly moved and touched to hear about the effect that hearing about kidney donations had on her.
sentences.zh: 听到肾脏捐赠的故事对她产生的影响，我感到非常感动和触动。

sentences.en: Going back to the very first person that we know of who for sure wanted to donate a kidney to a stranger, her name was Sinyana Graf.
sentences.zh: 回到我们所知的第一个确定想要向陌生人捐赠肾脏的人，她的名字叫辛亚娜·格拉夫（Sinyana Graf）。

sentences.en: And or I should say her name is Sinyana Graf.
sentences.zh: 或者我应该说，她的名字叫辛亚娜·格拉夫。

sentences.en: She's still alive.
sentences.zh: 她还健在。

sentences.en: And she had a very unusual story because unlike most of the altruistic kidney donors that I have worked with,
sentences.zh: 她的故事非常不寻常，因为与我合作过的大多数利他主义肾脏捐赠者不同，

sentences.en: whose decisions in part were a response to finding out about somebody else donating, which I think illustrates the incredible ripple effects that altruism has.
sentences.zh: 那些人的决定部分是受到他人捐赠行为的影响，我认为这说明了利他主义具有不可思议的连锁反应。

sentences.en: And she decided to donate, having never known anybody who had done it before.
sentences.zh: 而她决定捐赠时，从未认识任何做过这件事的人。

sentences.en: She simply knew that there was a need for kidneys, that it was possible to donate to somebody who was unrelated to you.
sentences.zh: 她只是知道有人需要肾脏，而且向非亲属捐赠是可能的。

sentences.en: And she was a mom and a Buddhist religious leader at the time who didn't have a lot of extra time or a lot of extra money to donate.
sentences.zh: 当时她是一位母亲，也是一位佛教宗教领袖，并没有太多的闲暇时间或多余的钱来捐赠。

sentences.en: And she thought, you know, I'm somebody who believes helping is an incredibly important part of a good life.
sentences.zh: 她想，你知道吗，我是一个相信帮助他人是美好生活极其重要一部分的人。

sentences.en: This is a way that I can help.
sentences.zh: 这是我可以提供帮助的一种方式。

sentences.en: And to her great credit, she was very persistent in tracking down a transplant facility that would actually do the transplant.
sentences.zh: 值得称赞的是，她非常执着地寻找愿意进行这种移植手术的机构。

sentences.en: Because at the time, most transplant facilities actually refused to let people donate a kidney to a stranger.
sentences.zh: 因为在当时，大多数移植机构实际上拒绝让人向陌生人捐赠肾脏。

sentences.en: So most people are much less generous towards strangers than they are towards close friends and family.
sentences.zh: 所以，大多数人对陌生人的慷慨程度远低于对亲朋好友的慷慨程度。

sentences.en: And this is a bias that's known as social discounting.
sentences.zh: 这种偏见被称为“社会折扣”（social discounting）。

sentences.en: But people who engage in extraordinary real-world altruism, like the altruistic kidney donors we've been talking about, show dramatically reduced social discounting.
sentences.zh: 但那些从事非凡现实利他行为的人，比如我们一直在谈论的利他主义肾脏捐赠者，表现出了显著降低的社会折扣。

sentences.en: In your research, you explored various explanations for reduced social discounting among these altruists.
sentences.zh: 在你的研究中，你探索了这些利他主义者社会折扣降低的各种解释。

sentences.en: What explanation did you rule out and which one did you settle on, Abby?
sentences.zh: 你排除了哪种解释，又最终确定了哪种解释，艾比？

sentences.en: So in our initial research with altruistic kidney donors, we discovered that they are, unlike most people, very generous to people who they don't know well,
sentences.zh: 在与利他主义肾脏捐赠者的初步研究中，我们发现，与大多数人不同，他们对不熟悉的人非常慷慨，

sentences.en: who are very different from themselves, who are even strangers.
sentences.zh: 对那些与自己截然不同的人，甚至是陌生人，也是如此。

sentences.en: And that makes sense.
sentences.zh: 这说得通。

sentences.en: If you're willing to give a kidney to a stranger, it makes sense that you don't discount the welfare of very distant others more.
sentences.zh: 如果你愿意向陌生人捐赠肾脏，那么你不会对非常疏远的人的福祉打折扣，这很合理。

sentences.en: The question is why?
sentences.zh: 问题是为什么？

sentences.en: And I will say there's a lot we still don't understand about why this happens.
sentences.zh: 我得说，关于为什么会发生这种情况，我们还有很多不了解的地方。

sentences.en: But there seem to be a couple things in mind.
sentences.zh: 但似乎有几点值得考虑。

sentences.en: First, at the most sort of simple mechanistic level, it's clear that altruistic kidney donors genuinely place more value on the welfare of other people, all other people,
sentences.zh: 首先，在最简单的机制层面上，很明显，利他主义肾脏捐赠者确实更看重他人的福祉，所有人的福祉，

sentences.en: and that the value that they place on others' welfare just doesn't drop off as those people become more socially distant from them.
sentences.zh: 而且他们对他人的福祉所赋予的价值，并不会随着这些人与他们在社会关系上的疏远而降低。

sentences.en: Meaning they genuinely believe that what happens to other people matters regardless of who those other people are.
sentences.zh: 这意味着他们真诚地相信，无论对方是谁，发生在他人身上的事都很重要。

sentences.en: It's possible that you could get an effect like that from people getting better and better at overriding the desire to be selfish as the desire to be selfish grows.
sentences.zh: 有一种可能，这种效果来自于人们在自私欲望增长时，越来越擅长抑制这种欲望。

sentences.en: And so maybe it could be the case that altruistic kidney donors are just very good at overriding the bias to be selfish when it comes to sharing with strangers.
sentences.zh: 所以也许利他主义肾脏捐赠者只是非常擅长在与陌生人分享时，克服自私的偏见。

sentences.en: But the brain imaging research we did showed no evidence of that at all.
sentences.zh: 但我们所做的脑成像研究完全没有证据支持这一点。

sentences.en: When we asked altruistic kidney donors and typical adults to make decisions whether to be selfish or to share with increasingly distant others during fMRI brain scanning,
sentences.zh: 当我们要求利他主义肾脏捐赠者和普通成年人在功能性磁共振成像（fMRI）扫描期间，决定是自私还是与日益疏远的人分享时，

sentences.en: we found no evidence of activation in any of the brain regions that are associated with overcoming internal biases, including the bias to be selfish.
sentences.zh: 我们没有发现任何与克服内在偏见（包括自私偏见）相关的大脑区域有激活迹象。

sentences.en: Instead,
sentences.zh: 相反，

sentences.en: we found patterns of activation in regions like the amygdala and the rostralian teres cingulate cortex that mapped on to the value that the altruists were placing on increasingly distant strangers' welfare.
sentences.zh: 我们在杏仁核和喙前扣带回等区域发现了激活模式，这些模式与利他主义者对日益疏远的陌生人的福祉所赋予的价值相对应。

sentences.en: Lucia mentioned in her message to us that she believes that God put us on Earth to help other people.
sentences.zh: 露西亚在给我们的留言中提到，她相信上帝把我们放在地球上是为了帮助他人。

sentences.en: This brings us to a question that many people raised.
sentences.zh: 这引出了许多人提出的一个问题。

sentences.en: Here's a message we received from listener Bob Dean.
sentences.zh: 这是我们收到的一条来自听众鲍勃·迪恩（Bob Dean）神父的留言。

sentences.en: Hello, my name is Father Bob Dean from Holy Family Church in Duxbury, Massachusetts.
sentences.zh: 你好，我是来自马萨诸塞州达克斯伯里圣家堂的鲍勃·迪恩神父。

sentences.en: And I'm calling to ask the question, is there any correlation between religiosity and one's altruism?
sentences.zh: 我打电话是想问，宗教信仰与一个人的利他主义之间是否存在某种相关性？

sentences.en: What do you think, Abby?
sentences.zh: 你怎么看，艾比？

sentences.en: The relationship between religiosity and altruism is complex.
sentences.zh: 宗教信仰与利他主义之间的关系很复杂。

sentences.en: There's no question that most major religious faiths place a lot of value on helping strangers,
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，大多数主要宗教信仰都非常重视帮助陌生人，

sentences.en: with the parable of the Good Samaritan potentially being the most obvious example.
sentences.zh: “好撒马利亚人”的比喻可能是最明显的例子。

sentences.en: Jesus makes it extremely clear in his teachings that all of us have the obligation to care for our neighbor,
sentences.zh: 耶稣在教导中非常明确地指出，我们所有人都有照顾邻居的义务，

sentences.en: and that neighbor could be anybody, including people from groups that we traditionally don't like or even in conflict with.
sentences.zh: 而邻居可以是任何人，包括那些我们传统上不喜欢，甚至与之有冲突的群体的人。

sentences.en: And many other religions have very similar teachings.
sentences.zh: 许多其他宗教也有非常相似的教导。

sentences.en: Buddhism is one, Judaism, Islam, etc.
sentences.zh: 佛教是其中之一，还有犹太教、伊斯兰教等等。

sentences.en: However, if you look at altruistic behavior across groups of people,
sentences.zh: 然而，如果你观察不同群体间的利他行为，

sentences.en: you don't see as strong a relationship as you might expect between either religiosity and altruism
sentences.zh: 你会发现宗教信仰与利他主义之间，或者特定的宗教信仰与从事利他行为之间，并没有你预期的那么强烈的关系，当然也有一些例外。

sentences.en: or a specific religious faith and engaging in altruistic behaviors, with some exceptions.
sentences.zh: 所以，例如在伊斯兰教这样的信仰中，一年中有某些时期，向他人捐赠是那个时期的传统，

sentences.en: So, for example, in a faith like Islam, where there are certain times of year where giving to others is sort of the tradition during that time period,
sentences.zh: 你绝对会看到捐赠的大幅增加。

sentences.en: you absolutely see big increases in giving.
sentences.zh: 但纵观全年，差异并没有那么巨大。

sentences.en: But over the course of the year, the differences are not that huge.
sentences.zh: 如果任何社区在“我们这类人”和“非我们这类人”之间制造了隔阂，

sentences.en: And to the degree that any community creates a division between those who are like us and those who are not like us,
sentences.zh: 那实际上会抑制利他主义和慷慨。

sentences.en: that can actually suppress altruism and generosity.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，在一些宗教社区中确实存在这种倾向，这适用于许多信仰，

sentences.en: And so, unfortunately, there is a tendency in some religious communities, and this applies to many faiths,
sentences.zh: 即明确表示，那些真正重要的人是遵循我们相同信仰和传统的人，

sentences.en: to make it clear that the people whose outcomes really matter are the people who follow the same beliefs and traditions we do,
sentences.zh: 而那些不遵循的人，则无关紧要。

sentences.en: and people who don't, don't matter.
sentences.zh: 这实际上抑制了利他主义。

sentences.en: And so that actually suppresses altruism.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，在这种关系中存在许多相互竞争的力量。

sentences.en: And so I think there's a lot of sort of competing forces that play into that relationship.
sentences.zh: 我的感觉是，如果你的特定宗教观点与“人具有内在的善良”这一理念相一致，

sentences.en: My sense is, to the degree that your specific religious views are consistent with the idea that there is inherent goodness in people
sentences.zh: 并且认为普通人是值得帮助的，即使你对他们了解不多，

sentences.en: and that the average person is worth helping, even if you don't know much about them,
sentences.zh: 那么这可能会在宗教信仰和利他主义之间建立起一种联系。

sentences.en: then that could create a relationship between religiosity and altruism.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 你在我们最初的谈话中与听众分享的信息之一是，

sentences.en: One of the messages that you shared with our audience in our initial conversation
sentences.zh: 我们无法通过训练让自己变得更利他。

sentences.en: is that we cannot train ourselves to be more altruistic.
sentences.zh: 一位名叫苏西（Susie）的听众提出了一个问题，涉及是否可能存在相反的情况。

sentences.en: A listener named Susie had a question that touches on whether the opposite might also be true.
sentences.zh: 这是苏西的留言。

sentences.en: Here's Susie.
sentences.zh: 当时我作为一名护士，凌晨3点半开车回家，

sentences.en: I was in a situation working as a nurse driving home at 3.30 in the morning
sentences.zh: 在科罗拉多州丹佛市的马路中间发现了一名女子，时值二月，

sentences.en: and found a woman in the middle of the road, February, in Denver, Colorado,
sentences.zh: 她在外面冻得发抖，赤身裸体，浑身是伤，满身是血。

sentences.en: freezing outside, naked, beaten and bloody.
sentences.zh: 我靠边停车，把她扶到路边，

sentences.en: Pulled over, helped her to the side of the road,
sentences.zh: 用我车里的一个暖和睡袋把她裹起来，等待救护车。

sentences.en: wrapped her in a warm sleeping bag I had in my car, waited for the ambulance.
sentences.zh: 那时我27岁。

sentences.en: I was 27 at the time when that happened.
sentences.zh: 现在我60岁了。

sentences.en: Now I'm 60.
sentences.zh: 我想知道你的杏仁核是否会随时间发生变化。

sentences.en: And I wonder if your amygdala changes over time.
sentences.zh: 它的大小会变吗？

sentences.en: Does the size change?
sentences.zh: 经历会改变这种反应吗？

sentences.en: Does experience change that response?
sentences.zh: 并不是说我今天不会做同样的事，

sentences.en: Not saying I wouldn't do the same thing today,
sentences.zh: 只是想知道人生经历和对恐惧的接触是否会随时间改变你的反应。

sentences.en: just wondering if life experience, exposure to fear changes your reaction over time.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 那么，艾比，苏西提到了大脑中被称为杏仁核的部分。

sentences.en: So, Abby, Susie referenced a part of the brain known as the amygdala.
sentences.zh: 在我们之前的谈话中，我们讨论了你的研究发现，

sentences.en: In our earlier conversation, we talked about your research finding that people
sentences.zh: 那些异常关心他人且高度利他的人平均拥有更大的杏仁核，

sentences.en: who are unusually caring and highly altruistic have larger amygdalas on average,
sentences.zh: 这可能就是他们能够更好地识别他人痛苦的原因。

sentences.en: and this might be why they are better able to recognize the distress of other people.
sentences.zh: 你对苏西的问题怎么看？

sentences.en: What do you think of Susie's question?
sentences.zh: 经历恐惧会让你变得更厌恶风险吗？

sentences.en: Can experiencing fear make you more risk-averse?
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，并不会。

sentences.en: Interestingly, no.
sentences.zh: 有一些非常酷的数据，特别是在疫情期间，

sentences.en: There is really cool data, especially from the pandemic,
sentences.zh: 表明急性压力状态似乎使人们更有可能帮助他人，

sentences.en: that states of acute stress seem to make people even more likely to help others,
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一种非常美妙的道德启示，

sentences.en: which I think is sort of a really wonderful moral,
sentences.zh: 因为我确实认为引人入胜的小说作品，

sentences.en: because I do think compelling works of fiction,
sentences.zh: 例如《蝇王》，

sentences.en: like, for example, The Lord of the Flies,
sentences.zh: 描绘了一幅人们处于文明边缘摇摇欲坠的画面，

sentences.en: paint a picture of people just sort of teetering on the brink of civility,
sentences.zh: 一旦情况开始恶化，

sentences.en: and the moment things start to go south
sentences.zh: 我们都在经历恐惧和压力，

sentences.en: and we're all experiencing a lot of fear and stress,
sentences.zh: 我们就会自相残杀。

sentences.en: we're going to turn on each other.
sentences.zh: 我们就会自相残杀。

sentences.en: But the reality doesn't seem to bear that out.
sentences.zh: 但现实似乎并不支持这一点。

sentences.en: In fact, there has been a case study of a real Lord of the Flies situation
sentences.zh: 事实上，曾有一个关于现实版《蝇王》情境的案例研究，

sentences.en: in which a group of boys, I think from Australia,
sentences.zh: 当时有一群男孩，我想是来自澳大利亚，

sentences.en: but it was certainly somewhere in the South Pacific,
